title: SLO decomposition and anomaly breadcrumbs index for burn-rate RCA
creator: Ava Patel
description: Create an index and runtime workflow that decomposes SLO burn-rate alerts into a ranked set of cross-signal breadcrumbs (traces, metric spikes, log-excerpts, dashboard snapshots). Goal is to reduce mean time to root cause for burn-rate incidents from minutes to < 15m and to provide deterministic handoffs to oncall and follow-up RCA owners.
acceptance_criteria: When a burn-rate alert fires, the incident page must include an ordered breadcrumb list: 1) top offending span groups, 2) metric deltas and percentiles, 3) representative log snippets, 4) dashboard snapshot links
Breadcrumbs must be generated within 90s of the alert and be reproducible (same inputs -> same ranked list)
Provide a /incidents API endpoint for automation that returns breadcrumbs as a JSON array of references (trace IDs, metric queries, log snippets, dashboard URLs)
Oncall playbook link and suggested next-step action must be surfaced on the incident card
End-to-end tests cover trace correlation, metric join correctness, and snapshot rendering under synthetic load
implementation_notes: Add lightweight span fingerprinting in trace-ingester to generate candidate span groups within 30s windows
Extend metric pipeline to compute delta-percentiles for SLO windows and expose top-k signals via a new proto (SignalCandidate)
Implement a joiner that correlates span groups with metric deltas and top log excerpts using time proximity and request-id affinity
Create a minimal templated dashboard snapshot renderer that accepts query refs and returns a short-lived URL (TTL 24h)
Cache breadcrumb bundles in Redis for fast retrieval by incident UI and automation bots
monitoring_queries: Log join heuristic: select log lines where request_id in (trace.request_ids) ordered by error_keyword_score desc limit 5
activity_log: 2026-02-18: Ticket created by Ava Patel. Initial scope and goals defined.
2026-02-23: Spike completed by Marcus Liu. Verified feasibility of span fingerprinting with <5% ingestion overhead (notes: spike/trace-fingerprint.md)
2026-03-02: Design review with PM and Observability leads. Decided to keep breadcrumb ranking deterministic and explainable rather than ML-blackbox for first rollout.
2026-03-05: UX sketches reviewed. Need a compact incident card that surfaces 3 breadcrumbs before fold and full list in detail pane.
2026-03-10: Engineering implementation started. Submitted initial proto and ingestion changes (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/4521)

2026-03-12: Integration test failing intermittently in CI due to race when cache invalidation overlaps ingestion. Identified fix: add versioned keys to Redis bundles. Assigned follow-up task ENG-308777.
risks: Increased ingestion cost if span fingerprinting retention not tuned
False positives in breadcrumb ranking could distract oncall; mitigation: conservative thresholds and human review during canary
Cache staleness could show incorrect bundles; mitigation: short TTL and versioned keys
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary, 2% traffic): enable breadcrumb generation for internal services only and collect metrics on generation latency and relevance
Phase 2 (org-internal): expand to all internal production services and add UI hooks for oncall feedback
Phase 3 (customer opt-in): expose feature flag in Console for Dedicated/Private customers, document privacy implications for log snippets
Fallback: if breadcrumbs generation fails, incident surface will show standard metric-only burn-rate card and link to raw traces
pager_policy_change: Proposed change: for burn-rate alerts that include a high-confidence breadcrumb (>= 3 correlated signals), page primary oncall. For low-confidence (1 signal or low matching score), create an incident but only notify via Slack channel and assign to SRE triage queue.
